# Python source selection interface vectors

These original public synthetic expectations supplement the unchanged shared
source JSON, canonical-number and original JSON Pointer packages under
`crates/arboresce-domain/tests/fixtures/` in this repository. They are not model,
human, service, recovery or production qualification.

Exact bytes/string intake rejects mutable buffers, other types and subclasses
before any caller conversion callback. Unpaired pointer surrogates are rejected.
Complete original admission precedes even an invalid supplied pointer. The pure
Python interface returns static failure enum values so expected rejection does
not expose a traceback/context that retains input.

Normal construction and mutation cannot install unchecked source or result
state. Immutable results expose canonical bytes, UTF-8 length and 32-byte SHA-256;
copy operations retain the same immutable value. Debug text is redacted. Private
reflection and caller-created values confer no admission or authority.

Freeze and independently review these literals before consumer implementation.
Helpers reconstruct inputs and report actual outcomes without expected answers;
assertions compare the separately retained literals. Original shared source,
decimal, UTF-16, pointer, property/mutation and exact/one-over meanings remain.
Actual current source/helper/static/process/strict coverage and independent
delivery gates remain required before this reference is qualified.

The `recipes` table freezes input construction, hostile callback methods and
their reset boundary, constructor attempts, named mutation targets, exact
`vars()` operations, copy setup, equality operand and byte mutation. Every
constructor attempt must reject independently. Successful byte and digest
getters return exact built-in `bytes`. Recipes are declarative review input;
test helpers implement a closed dispatch and never execute fixture text.

The private key adapter supplement fixes coherent identity equality, inequality
and reflected comparisons, sealed construction/mutation and immutable ordinal
hashes. Reverse-ordered object recipes cover empty/one/maximum selected objects
and both sides of every actual fresh dictionary resize. Nested equal-text keys
at different object ordinals retain ordinary JSON content. The original shared
Unicode, UTF-16 and duplicate cases remain mandatory. No private adapter or tree
is exposed by the processing API. Source-tag path reasoning alone is not
installed-binary, allocation, work or native qualification.

The public `recipe_contract` defines indexed keys as the exact prefix followed
by six-digit zero-padded decimal indices starting at zero. Compact punctuation,
literal value tokens, empty objects and reverse-only member order are explicit.
Source and separately frozen expected recipes use the declared order directly;
expansion never discovers a canonical answer from a consumer.

The four resource vectors additionally cover exact10MiB wide escaped string
and object-key output, an otherwise-valid selected output one byte over with
the original eleven bytes below its cap, and65535selected members sharing a
long wide prefix. Independent source/expected byte recipes and literal hashes
precede test consumption. They target regex chunk/header overlap, Unicode
promotion, member comparison and private full-object work; passing them alone
does not establish a universal allocation, RSS or native-stack bound.
